Featured [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/info/Features/John-Tizya-centre-feature.jpg?modified=20221121210502)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/visit/serv/tizya) ### [The John Tizya Centre](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/visit/serv/tizya) Take a tour of the exhibits, listen to audio recordings of elders’ stories, admire traditional tools, learn about the magnificent Porcupine Caribou Herd, and find out what life was like in the ancient Beringian landscapes of the last ice age. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/info/Features/Old-Crow-Flats-feature.jpg?modified=20221121210503)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/nature/habitats) ### [Van Tat - Old Crow Flats](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/nature/habitats) The Old Crow Flats is a vast wetland complex of shallow lakes and small streams, important to the Vuntut Gwitchin for subsistence hunting and other traditional practices. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/info/Features/PCH-feature.jpg?modified=20221121210502)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/nature/caribou) ### [Porcupine caribou herd](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/nature/caribou) The Porcupine Caribou Herd is one of the largest caribou herds in North America. The herd is central to the culture and way of life of the Vuntut Gwitchin. ## Visiting Vuntut National Park ### [Activities and experiences](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/activ) Things to do, explore Old Crow, the John Tizya Centre, arctic adventure ### [Plan your visit](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/visit) How to get here, facilities and services, park regulations, maps. ### [Safety and guidelines](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety) Vuntut National Park is a remote wilderness park. Visitors must be self-reliant and have the equipment and skills to travel safely in an isolated arctic... ## About Vuntut National Park ### [Culture and history](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/culture) For countless generations, the Vuntut Gwitchin have lived in the Old Crow Flats and Porcupine River areas in the northern Yukon. ### [Nature and science](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/nature) Conservation and science, animals, plants, the environment, and research. ### [Stewardship and management](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/gestion-management) Cooperative Management, Management Plan, commercial film and photography permits [×Dismiss](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut# "Dismiss") +− ⇧ - © [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright) contributors. i ? | Zoom to element | Type | Location text | Location name | Address | Select | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Check to select the element on the map | 1 | Vuntut National Park | Vuntut National Park |

Vuntut National Park is approximately 50 km by air or 190 km by river north of Old Crow, Yukon.


Plan your visit

| | [How to get here](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/visit) ### Contact us Box 19 Old Crow YT  Y0B 1N0 Phone number:867-966-3622 Email address:[pc.vuntutinfo.pc@canada.ca](mailto:pc.vuntutinfo.pc@canada.ca) ### Hours of operation **Telephone:** Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm (PST): (867) 966-3622 **John Tizya Centre** **in Old Crow** Monday to Friday, 9:00am-12:00pm and 1:00pm-4:30pm ### Social - [Facebook](https://facebook.com/ParksCanadaYukon/) - [Twitter](https://x.com/ParksCanYukon) ## More places to discover with Parks Canada [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/yt/yt-kluane-pn-np-640x360.jpg?modified=20221125212558)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/kluane) ### [Kluane National Park and Reserve](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/kluane) With vast icefields and 17 of Canada’s 20 highest peaks, Kluane offers outstanding alpine scenery, rich First Nations culture and history, and a mix of extreme adventure and accessible outdoor recreation. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/yt/yt-ivvavik-pn-np-640x360.jpg?modified=20221125213622)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/ivvavik) ### [Ivvavik National Park](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/ivvavik) Rafters from around the world meet up in Ivvavik National Park. The Firth River slices through canyons and mountain valleys to the Arctic Ocean.  A fly-in base camp offers hikers access to an Arctic landscape of tors, peaks and rolling hills untouched by the last Ice Age. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/yt/yt-chilkoot-lhn-nhs-640x360.jpg?modified=20221125212558)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/yt/chilkoot) ### [Chilkoot Trail National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/yt/chilkoot) Hike a legendary trail through the northern Coast Mountains, from Alaska’s Taiya Inlet to the headwaters of the Yukon River in northern British Columbia. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/yt/yt-ss-klondike-lhn-nhs-640x360.jpg?modified=20221125212558)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/yt/ssklondike) ### [S.S. Klondike National Historic Site](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/yt/ssklondike) Steam-powered sternwheelers were the Yukon’s link to the outside world for almost a century. The S.S. Klondike National Historic Site in Whitehorse honours these vessels, so vital to the settlement of the North. [![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/WET4/proximite-nearby/yt/yt-klondike-lhn-nhs-640x360.jpg?modified=20221125212558)](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/yt/klondike) ### [Klondike National Historic Sites](https://parks.canada.ca/lhn-nhs/yt/klondike) Step back into the days of the 1898 Klondike Gold Rush. Prowl a paddlewheeler. Explore goldfields. Magical Dawson City is a frontier town where history mingles with everyday life. Date modified : 2024-08-18

# Visitor safety

## Vuntut National Park

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/securite-safety/Safety-weather.jpg?modified=20170213184836)\\
\\
Weather](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/securite-safety/bears-J-Peter.jpg?modified=20170213184827)\\
\\
Wildlife](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/securite-safety/Safety-wilderness-J-Peter.jpg?modified=20170213184849)\\
\\
Wilderness setting](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

Careful trip planning and preparation are essential to safe enjoyment of Vuntut’s spectacular backcountry. Vuntut National Park is a remote wilderness park with no facilities, services, designated landing areas, or developed trails. Basic rescue services may take days to arrive. Park visitors must be self-reliant and have the required equipment, knowledge, skills and physical fitness to travel safely in an isolated arctic environment and be able to handle any medical or wildlife related emergencies on their own.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/securite-safety/Safety-weather.jpg?modified=20170213184836)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

### [Weather](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

Weather is the most significant hazard for visitors to Vuntut. It is variable and can change quickly.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/securite-safety/bears-J-Peter.jpg?modified=20170213184827)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

### [Wildlife](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

Wildlife encounters can pose serious threats to visitor safety. Encounters with grizzly bears, black bears, muskox, caribou and moose with calves, all present potential risks.

[![](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/yt/vuntut/WET4/securite-safety/Safety-wilderness-J-Peter.jpg?modified=20170213184849)](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

### [Wilderness setting](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/yt/vuntut/securite-safety/sec-saf)

Know the risks of travelling on the park’s terrain, and be aware that the geographic isolation of the park can compound the severity of any incident.

You are responsible for your own safety. You should _:_

- Be self-reliant.

- Have the required equipment, knowledge, skills and physical fitness for a safe trip.

- Consider public safety information and advice provided by Parks Canada.

- Seek out additional knowledge and advice from Vuntut Gwitchin of Old Crow who are very familiar with the land and waters of the park.

- Comply with the public safety registration and de-registration program.

- Be prepared for medical, wildlife, and weather-related emergencies and able to handle all emergencies on your own. Help could be days away.

- Have multiple communication devices such as a SPOT device, satellite phone, and or satellite pager with back-up power sources.


All visitors to Vuntut are required to register prior to starting their trip and to de-register on completion of their trip. This information will aid in search and rescue efforts should they be needed. Failure to register or deregister is an offence under the National Park Regulations.

**Parks Canada 24 Hour Emergency Dispatch**

1-780-852-3100 (can be dialled from a satellite phone)
